title: applied-ml-experiment-scratchpad-2026-03-04-jordan-patel-2
content:
Daily scratchpad - applied ML experiments (quick brain dump)
Date: 2026-03-04
Owner: Jordan Patel

---
Morning goals:
- finish int8-int4 baseline runs for redwood-v0-7 on A100-40GB pool
- sanity check eval harness on curated prompt set (chat+instruction)
- note any regressions from 2026-03-02 run

Runs summary (fast notes):
1) model redwood-v0-7 / fp16 (baseline)
   - batch=1, seq=1024, temperature=0.0 (deterministic eval)
   - avg latency (token): 28ms/token (p95: 45ms) on a100-40
   - LL / ppl on eval_prompts_v2: 2.14 / 9.5

2) model redwood-v0-7 / int8 (quantize per-channel, post-training)
   - same config, avg latency: 18ms/token (p95: 30ms)
   - LL: 2.23 (delta +0.09) — small degradation but acceptable for chat responses
   - embedding cos-sim on semantic dataset: mean 0.986 -> 0.981 (drop ~0.5%)

3) model redwood-v0-7 / int4 (experimental, GPTQ-like)
   - avg latency: 14ms/token (p95: 22ms)
   - LL: 2.6 (delta +0.46) — noticeable quality drop on long-form completion
   - open issues: truncation artifacts for prefix lengths >512; need KV-cache alignment check

Quick notes on quant pipeline:
- used quantize_tool v0.9 (PR #512) from serving-runtime; ensure conversion flags: --sym-clip false --per-channel true
- potential bug: int4 run uses legacy KV cache stride; file a follow-up if p95 divergence persists (linked PR above)
- TODO: re-run int4 with --align-kv=64 and compare

Prompt/eval set notes (eval_prompts_v2):
- contains 420 prompts across categories: summarization (100), instruction-following (150), multi-turn chat (120), code (50)
- observed higher error rate in code prompts for int4: test-suite failure rate 7% -> 18%
- hypothesis: quantization affects identifier/tokenization mapping for code tokens; try 8-bit fallback for rare tokens

Experiment checklist (short-term):
- [ ] re-run int4 with KV align flag (--align-kv=64) on 2 GPUs (A100-80) to see if artifacts persist
- [ ] add token-level diff script to compare fp16 vs int4 outputs for sample set (20 pairs)
- [ ] run a human eval quick-sweep (Asha/Maya) on 30 chat prompts to validate perceived quality
- [ ] add an automated regression alert in optimize pipeline if LL delta > 0.2

Ops/commands I ran (local notes):
- convert: python tools/quantize.py --model redwood-v0-7 --bits 4 --per-channel --output /tmp/rw_v07_int4
- run eval: python eval/harness.py --model /tmp/rw_v07_int4 --prompts data/eval_prompts_v2.json --batch 1 --seq 1024 --out results/int4_run_2026-03-04.json
- quick stats: python tools/compute_metrics.py results/int4_run_2026-03-04.json --metrics ll,perplexity,embed_cos

Notes to self / loose ideas:
- consider hybrid quant: int4 on transformer blocks 0..L-3, int8 on last 3 blocks to preserve final-layer features (could help code generation)
- explore fp16->int8->int4 staged fine-tune (small LR) for critical tokens — expensive but might recover quality
- caching: try prefix caching experiment for conversational benchmark to reduce cold-start tokens (measure cost per convo)

Human eval plan (quick):
- owners: Asha (summaries + chat), Maya (code + instruction)
- sample: 30 prompts per category, blind A/B (fp16 vs int8 vs int4) randomized, bucket by token length
- metrics: helpfulness(1-5), correctness(1-5), hallucination flag (Y/N), prefered model
- timeline: run this week, results by Friday 2026-03-06

Known issues / blockers:
- GPU pool noisy neighbor on A100-40 observed spikes at 11:20-11:40 — correlate with infra autoscaler logs (ask infra team)
- int4 toolchain sometimes segfaults on conversion for specific checkpoint variants (checkpoint id: rw_v07_sharded-20260219), need to re-run with single shard

Links / refs:
- PR for quant tools: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/512
- Jira ticket (broader): ENG-2987 (quant-eval follow-ups)
- Eval config page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ML/pages/987654321/quant-eval-notes

End-of-day quick log:
- progress: int8 looks promising for hosted API tier (good latency win, small quality hit). int4 needs more work before we can recommend for production.
- blockers: KV alignment + segfaults. Human eval queued.

Random TODOs (tiny):
- ping @infra on slack about noisy neighbor (channel: #infra-gpu)
- add small note to product: potential offering - "cost-tiered models: int8 discounted hosted tier" (cc: product-hosted-api)
- cleanup results dir and archive old runs >30 days

---
Short-term next steps (tomorrow):
1) re-run int4 with align flag, capture logs, attach to ENG-2987
2) make token-diff script and run on 20 pairs
3) prepare human-eval job (Asha/Maya) and generate randomized A/B csv


(End of scratchpad)
